page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 2 virtual CPUs mapped to 1 physical core on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz with hyper-threading. Built on x86_64 architecture, it is configured with 16.0 GB of memory, delivering a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per virtual core. The processor includes 33 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache, alongside hardware instruction extensions such as AVX-512, AES, and FMA. This instance type includes no local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs.

In performance benchmarks, the single-core execution on the n2-highmem-2 demonstrates moderate capability, recording a stress-ng single-core score of 1827.69. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics reflect significant compute constraints due to its single-physical-core topology. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 2164.15 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1321.0. Large-block memory read bandwidth measures 13.86 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 11.77 GB/sec. Application benchmarks show Redis SET performance at 1.67 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 1.61 GB/sec.

The server hardware profile offers a cost-effective memory allocation relative to its low vCPU count, making it suited for workloads that require moderate memory footprints without demanding high CPU concurrency. The main tradeoff lies in limited multi-core processing throughput and low overall memory bandwidth under heavy loads. The n2-highmem-2 is best suited for light database caching, small in-memory stores, background memory-bound task queues, and low-traffic web serving applications.
